chapters.title: कारक — the roles a noun plays, and the case each takes

readings.translation: The man goes.
readings.teaches: bare कर्तृ + verb; the प्रथमा as the base case

notes.role: नर is the कर्तृ — the independent agent
प्रथमा for the bare prātipadika-sense → नरः
सुप्: सु (nom.sg) on नर

notes.text: नर + सु, then नरस् → नरः

notes.role: नरस्: final स → रु
रु → visarga before pause → नरः
वर्तमाने लट् — present tense

readings.vyakhya: नरः स्वतन्त्रः, अतः प्रथमा।
readings.vyakhya_en: The agent acting on its own stands in the प्रथमा — the base case. This is the starting point every other case departs from.

readings.translation: The man goes to the village.
readings.teaches: adds कर्मन् → द्वितीया

notes.role: ग्राम is कर्मन् — what the agent reaches
कर्मणि द्वितीया → ग्रामम्

readings.vyakhya: यत् कर्तुः ईप्सिततमम् तत् कर्मन्, कर्मणि द्वितीया।
readings.vyakhya_en: What the agent most wants to reach is the कर्मन्; the कर्मन् takes the द्वितीया. The goal of motion is reached, so it is कर्मन् — hence ग्रामम्.

readings.translation: The man goes to the village on foot.
readings.teaches: adds करण → तृतीया

notes.role: पाद is करण — the most effective means

notes.en: dual — a man has two feet

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → पादाभ्याम्

readings.vyakhya: पादौ साधकतमम् करण, कर्तृकरणयोः तृतीया।
readings.vyakhya_en: The feet are the most effective means by which the going is done — the करण — and the करण takes the तृतीया.

readings.translation: The man comes from the village.
readings.teaches: adds अपादान → पञ्चमी

notes.role: ग्राम is अपादान — the fixed point of departure
अपादाने पञ्चमी → ग्रामात्

notes.text: आ +

notes.en: "come" — आ adds "toward," motion toward the speaker

readings.vyakhya: ध्रुवम् अपाये अपादान, अपादाने पञ्चमी।
readings.vyakhya_en: The fixed point from which there is departure is the अपादान; it takes the पञ्चमी. Same word ग्राम — goal (द्वितीया) above, source (पञ्चमी) here. The case follows the role.

readings.translation: The man gives fruit to the boy.
readings.teaches: adds सम्प्रदान → चतुर्थी

notes.role: बाल is सम्प्रदान — the one aimed at, the recipient
चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → बालाय

readings.vyakhya: कर्मणा यम् अभिप्रैति सः सम्प्रदान, चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने।
readings.vyakhya_en: The one the agent aims at through the object — here, through the fruit, the boy — is the सम्प्रदान; it takes the चतुर्थी.

readings.translation: The man lives in the village.
readings.teaches: adds अधिकरण → सप्तमी

notes.role: ग्राम is अधिकरण — the locus of the action
सप्तम्यधिकरणे च → ग्रामे

readings.vyakhya: आधारः अधिकरण, सप्तमी अधिकरणे।
readings.vyakhya_en: The locus in which the action rests is the अधिकरण; it takes the सप्तमी. A third role for ग्राम: goal, source, and now locus — द्वितीया, पञ्चमी, सप्तमी.

readings.translation: The man's son lives in the village.
readings.teaches: adds षष्ठी (a relation, not a कारक)

words.gloss: of the man, the relation whose

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे — the remaining relation (genitive) → नरस्य

readings.vyakhya: कारकभिन्नः सम्बन्धः शेष, तत्र षष्ठी।
readings.vyakhya_en: A relation that is not one of the कारकas — here mere belonging, "of the man" — is शेष, "the rest," and takes the षष्ठी. Note नर has stepped out of the agent-role; पुत्र is now the कर्तृ.

readings.translation: The boy fears the wolves.
readings.teaches: special government: a verb of fearing makes the feared thing अपादान → पञ्चमी

words.gloss: of/from the wolves — the thing feared

notes.en: source — here, what one shrinks from

notes.role: भीत्रार्थानां भयहेतुः — with verbs of fearing, the cause of fear is अपादान
अपादाने पञ्चमी → वृकेभ्यः

readings.vyakhya: भयहेतुः अपादानम् — न तु कर्म। वृकेभ्यः बिभेति, न वृकान्।
readings.vyakhya_en: One might expect the feared thing to be the कर्मन् (the object fearing "reaches"). But Pāṇini names it अपादान — what one shrinks away from — so it takes the पञ्चमी, not the द्वितीया: वृकेभ्यः, not वृकान्. Knowing the verb tells you the case.

readings.translation: The man owes Devadatta a hundred.
readings.teaches: special government: √धारि 'owe' makes the creditor सम्प्रदान → चतुर्थी

notes.role: धारेरुत्तमर्णः — with √धारि (owe), the creditor (उत्तमर्ण) is सम्प्रदान
चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → देवदत्ताय

readings.vyakhya: उत्तमर्णः सम्प्रदानम्। यस्य ऋणं धार्यते सः सम्प्रदानम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The creditor — the one to whom the debt is owed — is the सम्प्रदान, just as a gift's recipient is. So देवदत्ताय (चतुर्थी), the same case as the boy received the fruit in. A specific verb extends a familiar role.

readings.translation: Homage to the gods.
readings.teaches: नमः and its companions (स्वस्ति, स्वाहा …) govern the चतुर्थी

notes.text: the word of salutation

notes.role: नमःस्वस्ति… — with नमः (and स्वस्ति, स्वाहा, स्वधा, अलम्, वषट्) the word takes चतुर्थी
चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → देवेभ्यः

readings.vyakhya: नमसा योगे चतुर्थी। नमो देवेभ्यः, न देवान्।
readings.vyakhya_en: A handful of fixed words — नमः foremost — govern the चतुर्थी by themselves, no verb needed. "नमो देवेभ्यः," homage to the gods (चतुर्थी), never देवान्. Learn the word, and its case comes with it.

readings.translation: The man studies for a month.
readings.teaches: duration and extent (काल, अध्वन्) in continuous connection take द्वितीया

notes.en: object — here, the span filled by the action

notes.role: कालाध्वनोरत्यन्तसंयोगे — a time-word (or distance) in unbroken connection takes द्वितीया

readings.vyakhya: अत्यन्तसंयोगे कालाध्वनोः द्वितीया। मासम् अधीते — कृत्स्नं कालम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: When an action fills a whole stretch of time or space without a break, that span stands in the द्वितीया: मासम् अधीते, "studies through a whole month." The accusative here measures extent, not an object reached.

readings.translation: The father comes with the son.
readings.teaches: सह "with" → the accompanying (subordinate) person takes तृतीया

notes.role: सहयुक्तेऽप्रधाने — with सह, the accompanying (non-principal) thing takes तृतीया

notes.text: the particle governing पुत्रेण

readings.vyakhya: सहयोगे अप्रधाने तृतीया। पिता प्रधानम्, पुत्रः अप्रधानम् — पुत्रेण सह।
readings.vyakhya_en: With सह "together," the secondary companion — not the principal actor — stands in the तृतीया: पुत्रेण सह "with the son." The father is principal (प्रधान, प्रथमा); the son accompanies (अप्रधान, तृतीया). The same case that named the instrument also names the companion.

readings.translation: A family [is sustained] by wealth.
readings.teaches: हेतु "cause, reason" → the cause takes तृतीया

notes.role: हेतौ — the word naming a cause takes तृतीया

notes.en: instrumental — here the sense "by reason of"

readings.vyakhya: हेतौ तृतीया। येन फलं साध्यते सः हेतुः — धनेन कुलम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: What brings a result about — the cause — takes the तृतीया: धनेन "by reason of wealth." This is the same case as the instrument करण, widened: the means by which, and the cause for which, share one form.

readings.translation: He goes to the village.
readings.teaches: गत्यर्थ — with a verb of motion, the goal (कर्म) takes द्वितीया

notes.en: the goal of motion is treated as the object

notes.role: कर्तुरीप्सिततमं कर्म → the most-desired goal is कर्मन्
गत्यर्थकर्मणि द्वितीयाचतुर्थ्यौ — with a motion-verb the goal takes द्वितीया (or चतुर्थी)

notes.text: ग्रामम् → ग्रामं (final म् → anusvāra before ग)

notes.role: वर्तमाने लट् → present

readings.vyakhya: गत्यर्थस्य धातोः कर्म गन्तव्यं द्वितीयायाम्। ग्रामो गन्तव्यः, अतः ग्रामम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: A verb of motion (गम् "go") makes its destination the कर्मन् — the goal one most wants to reach (1.4.49) — and that takes the accusative (2.3.12). So "go TO the village" is simply ग्रामम् (acc.), no preposition needed. The same rule allows चतुर्थी (a dative of goal) in Vedic and poetry; classical prose prefers द्वितीया.

readings.translation: He studies for a month.
readings.teaches: अत्यन्तसंयोग — unbroken extent of time/space takes द्वितीया

notes.en: extent — the span over which the action runs without break

notes.role: कालाध्वनोरत्यन्तसंयोगे — a word of time or distance spanning an unbroken stretch takes द्वितीया

readings.vyakhya: कालस्य अध्वनश्च अत्यन्तसंयोगे द्वितीया। मासम् इति कालपरिमाणम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: Duration and distance, when the action fills the whole stretch without a gap, stand in the accusative (2.3.5) — मासम् "(for) a month," क्रोशम् "(for) a krośa of road." Not "to a month" but "across the whole of it." This is why "he studies for a month" needs no "for": the bare accusative मासम् carries the span.

readings.translation: He comes with his son.
readings.teaches: सह — the accompanying (subordinate) word takes तृतीया

notes.en: here the तृतीया of accompaniment, not instrument

notes.role: सहयुक्तेऽप्रधाने — with सह, the accompanier (the non-principal) takes तृतीया

readings.vyakhya: सहयोगे अप्रधानं तृतीयायाम्। पिता प्रधानम्, पुत्रः अप्रधानः — अतः पुत्रेण।
readings.vyakhya_en: "With" (सह) puts the companion — the *subordinate* party, not the principal — in the instrumental (2.3.19). The father is the principal (he is the agent who comes); the son merely accompanies, so the son is पुत्रेण, तृतीया. One case (तृतीया) thus carries two senses you now hold: instrument (by) and accompaniment (with).

readings.translation: A family (is honored) on account of wealth.
readings.teaches: हेतु — the cause/motive takes तृतीया

words.gloss: on account of wealth, because of wealth

notes.en: cause — the reason for which something happens

notes.role: हेतौ — a word denoting the cause takes तृतीया (विद्यया यशः, धनेन कुलम्)

readings.vyakhya: हेतौ तृतीया। धनं हेतुः, तेन कुलम् उन्नतम् — धनेन।
readings.vyakhya_en: The cause or motive — "because of X" — takes the instrumental (2.3.23). विद्यया यशः "fame through learning," धनेन कुलम् "a family (raised) by wealth." It is the same तृतीया as instrument and accompaniment, now in a third sense: the reason. Note how much one case-ending does — the reader must read the *sense* from context, not the form alone.

readings.translation: Without wealth, (there is) sorrow.
readings.teaches: विना — "without" takes तृतीया (optionally पञ्चमी/द्वितीया)

notes.role: पृथग्विनानानाभिस्तृतीयान्यतरस्याम् — with पृथक्/विना/नाना the word takes तृतीया (also पञ्चमी, द्वितीया)

readings.vyakhya: विना-योगे तृतीया अन्यतरस्याम्। धनेन विना, धनाद् विना, धनं विना — त्रयं साधु।
readings.vyakhya_en: पृथक्, विना, and नाना — all meaning "apart / without" — govern the instrumental, *optionally* (अन्यतरस्याम्, 2.3.32); the genitive… no, the ablative (पञ्चमी) and accusative are also allowed. So धनेन विना = धनाद् विना = धनं विना, all correct. The optionality (विभाषा / अन्यतरस्याम्) is itself a feature to notice: Pāṇini often sanctions more than one form.

readings.translation: The mountain is far from the village.
readings.teaches: अपादान/पञ्चमी for separation-distance — "from"

notes.en: the fixed point from which distance is measured

notes.role: ध्रुवमपायेऽपादानम् — the fixed source-point is अपादान
अपादाने पञ्चमी → ग्रामात्
सप्तम्यधिकरणे च → दूरे (सप्तमी)

notes.text: पर्वतः → पर्वतो before the voiced द (visarga सन्धि)

readings.vyakhya: अपायस्य ध्रुवम् अपादानम्, तस्मिन् पञ्चमी। ग्रामो ध्रुवः, ततो दूरम् — ग्रामात्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The ablative (पञ्चमी) marks the fixed point one moves or measures *from* (1.4.24, 2.3.28). With words of distance — दूरे "far," अन्तिके "near" — the reference point stands in the ablative: ग्रामात् "from the village." You met पञ्चमी as "from" in विनयाद् याति; here it is spatial separation, the rule's core sense.

readings.translation: When the sun has risen, the lotus opens.
readings.teaches: सति सप्तमी — the locative absolute: one act marking the time of another

notes.en: the locative-absolute subject — its action marks the time

notes.role: यस्य च भावेन भावलक्षणम् — that whose action marks another's time takes सप्तमी

notes.en: a past participle (क्त), agreeing with सूर्ये in सप्तमी

notes.text: उद् + इ → उदित "risen"

readings.vyakhya: यस्य भावेन अन्यस्य भावः लक्ष्यते, तत्र सप्तमी — सति सप्तमी। सूर्ये उदिते इति कालः।
readings.vyakhya_en: The "locative absolute" (सति सप्तमी): when one event fixes the *time* of another, the first stands — subject and participle together — in the locative (2.3.37). सूर्ये उदिते "the sun having risen" = "when the sun rose." It is Sanskrit's compact "when / while" clause: a noun + participle in सप्तमी, needing no conjunction.

readings.translation: The man's doing / the deed of the man.
readings.teaches: कृत्-योग — with a कृत् noun, agent & object take षष्ठी

notes.en: the agent, but expressed through षष्ठी before a कृत् noun

notes.role: कर्तृकर्मणोः कृति — before a कृत्-formed word, agent and object take षष्ठी

notes.en: a कृत् noun (action-noun in क्तिन्) from कृ "do"

notes.role: स्त्रियां क्तिन् — the feminine action-noun in क्तिन् → कृति

readings.vyakhya: कृति उपपदे कर्तृकर्मणोः षष्ठी। नरः कर्ता, कृतिः कृत्, अतः नरस्य कृतिः।
readings.vyakhya_en: When the head word is a कृत्-derivative (an action- or agent-noun built from a root), its agent and object are expressed by the genitive, not their usual cases (2.3.65). नरस्य कृतिः = "the man's deed" — नर is logically the doer, but before कृति (a कृत् noun) it takes षष्ठी. This is why "the seeing of the lotus" is कमलस्य दर्शनम्: the कृत् noun pulls everything into the genitive.

chapters.title: सुप् — nominal declension: stem-classes × विभक्ति × वचन

readings.translation: The boy sees the fruit.
readings.teaches: neuter stem फल: प्रथमा = द्वितीया (same frame, new declension)

notes.text: here प्रथमा and द्वितीया share one form, both फलम्

notes.role: अतोऽम् — neuter a-stem सु/अम् → अम्, so nom.sg फलम्
स्वमोर्नपुंसकात् — neuter सु and अम् behave alike: फलम् serves as both प्रथमा and द्वितीया

readings.vyakhya: नपुंसके प्रथमा द्वितीया च समाने रूपे — फलम् इति।
readings.vyakhya_en: In the neuter, प्रथमा and द्वितीया share one form. So फलम् is the कर्मन् here exactly as it would be the कर्तृ — the role still picks the case, but neuter collapses the two.

readings.translation: The fruit falls from the tree.
readings.teaches: neuter फलम् as कर्तृ (प्रथमा = द्वितीया form); reuses अपादान पञ्चमी

notes.role: फल is now कर्तृ — the same neuter form फलम् fills the agent role

notes.text: the neuter form is still फलम्

notes.role: अपादाने पञ्चमी → वृक्षात्

readings.vyakhya: फलम् इह स्वतन्त्रः कर्ता, तथापि रूपम् तदेव।
readings.vyakhya_en: The same word फलम् that was the object above is the agent here — and looks identical, because the neuter does not distinguish them. The अपादान-पञ्चमी (वृक्षात्) is exactly as it was for ग्रामात्: the frame is unchanged.

readings.translation: The man sees fruit in the river.
readings.teaches: feminine ī-stem नदी: अधिकरण सप्तमी नद्याम्, with यण् sandhi

notes.role: सप्तम्यधिकरणे च → नद्याम् (the locus)
स्त्रियाम् — the feminine, opening the stems नदी belongs to
ऋन्नेभ्यो ङीप् — नदी is a ङीप्-formed ī-stem feminine

notes.text: नदी + आम्

notes.role: ङेराम्नद्याम्नीभ्यः — ī-stem fem locative sg takes आम्: नदी+आम्

notes.text: → नद्याम्

notes.role: इको यणचि — ई before आम् becomes य्: नदी+आम् → नद्याम्

readings.vyakhya: अधिकरणे सप्तमी — स्त्रीलिङ्गेऽपि सैव।
readings.vyakhya_en: The locus takes the सप्तमी whatever the gender: ग्रामे (masc.) and नद्याम् (fem.) are the same case, differently declined. Role fixes the case; stem-class fixes the ending.

readings.translation: The two men go to the village.
readings.teaches: number: dual कर्तृ नरौ + dual verb

notes.role: द्व्येकयोर्द्विवचनैकवचने — two referents → द्विवचन (dual): नरौ, गच्छतः

notes.en: dual — the verb agrees with नरौ

readings.vyakhya: द्वयोः द्विवचनम् — कर्तरि क्रियायाम् च।
readings.vyakhya_en: Two referents call for the द्विवचन — in the noun (नरौ) and, agreeing, in the verb (गच्छतः). The role is still कर्तृ-प्रथमा, exactly as नरः was; only the count has changed.

readings.translation: The men go to the village.
readings.teaches: number: plural कर्तृ नराः (नर+जस् → नराः) + plural verb

notes.role: बहुषु बहुवचनम् — many referents → बहुवचन (plural)

notes.text: नर + जस् → नराः

notes.role: प्रथमयोः पूर्वसवर्णः — नर + जस् (अस्) → नराः, the nom.pl

readings.vyakhya: बहूनाम् बहुवचनम्। एकः नरः, द्वौ नरौ, बहवः नराः — एकैव विभक्तिः, भिद्यते वचनम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: Many referents call for the बहुवचन. नरः, नरौ, नराः — one प्रथमा case across three numbers: the विभक्ति is constant, the वचन varies.

readings.translation: The fruits are eaten by the men.
readings.teaches: plural instrumental नरैः (अ+भिस् → ऐस्) + neuter plural फलानि

notes.en: here the agent of a passive verb, in the instrumental

notes.text: नर + भिस् → नरैः

notes.role: अतो भिस ऐस् — a-stem instrumental plural भिस् → ऐस्: नर+ऐस् → नरैः

notes.text: फल → फलानि

notes.role: जश्शसोः शिः — neuter जस्/शस् → शि (इ): फल+शि
नपुंसकस्य झलचः — नुम् inserted before the शि-ending: फल+न्+इ
सर्वनामस्थाने चासम्बुद्धौ — the stem vowel lengthens: फला-न्-इ → फलानि

readings.vyakhya: बहुषु नरेषु करणभूतेषु तृतीया बहुवचनम्; फलानि नपुंसकबहुवचने।
readings.vyakhya_en: The instrumental plural नरैः; the neuter plural फलानि. Same roles as ever — only the number is new, and each stem-class spells the plural its own way.

readings.translation: The fire blazes.
readings.teaches: an इ-stem masculine: nominative अग्निः (नर-like सु, but on an इ-stem)

notes.text: अग्नि + सु → अग्निः

readings.vyakhya: इकारान्तं पुंलिङ्गम् अग्निशब्दः। प्रथमायाम् अग्निः, यथा नरः।
readings.vyakhya_en: अग्नि is a masculine stem ending in इ. In the प्रथमा it takes the same सु that नर did, giving अग्निः — outwardly like नरः. The stem-class shows itself not here but in the oblique cases, where the इ shifts.

readings.translation: The man gives water to the fire.
readings.teaches: the इ-stem dative अग्नये — the stem इ takes गुण (इ → ए) before the ending

notes.role: चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → the recipient अग्नि takes चतुर्थी
घेर्ङिति — before a ङित् ending (here ङे, the dative), the इ-stem takes गुण; अग्नि + ए → अग्नये

readings.vyakhya: घेः ङिति गुणः। अग्नि + ए → अग्नये — इकारस्य गुणः एकारः।
readings.vyakhya_en: Where नर simply added its ending (नराय), the इ-stem first shifts its इ to the गुण grade ए before the dative: अग्नि → अग्नय् + ए → अग्नये. Same case, same role as बालाय — but the stem-vowel changes, which is what marks the इ-class.

readings.translation: The fires blaze.
readings.teaches: the इ-stem nominative plural अग्नयः — again गुण before the plural ending

notes.role: जसि च — before जस् (nom.pl), the short इ-stem takes गुण; अग्नि + अस् → अग्नय् + अस् → अग्नयः

readings.vyakhya: जसि गुणः। अग्नि + अस् → अग्नयः, यथा चतुर्थ्याम् अग्नये।
readings.vyakhya_en: The same गुण appears in the nominative plural: अग्नि + जस् → अग्नयः ("the fires"), where नर gave नराः. The इ-stem reveals its character wherever an ending pulls the इ up to ए.

readings.translation: The father comes home.
readings.teaches: an ऋ-stem nominative: पिता (the ऋ → आ in the nom.sg)

notes.role: ऋदुशनस्… — an ऋ-stem in the nom.sg lengthens to आ; पितृ + सु → पिता

readings.vyakhya: ऋकारान्तस्य सौ आकारः। पितृ → पिता।
readings.vyakhya_en: An ऋ-stem — the class of kinship words (पितृ, मातृ, भ्रातृ) and agent-nouns (कर्तृ "doer") — shows आ in the nominative singular: पितृ → पिता, "the father." Where नर gave नरः and अग्नि gave अग्निः, the ऋ-stem ends in a bare long आ.

readings.translation: He sees the father.
readings.teaches: the ऋ-stem strong stem पितर् — ऋ takes गुण (अर्) in the strong cases

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → the object पितृ takes द्वितीया
ऋतो ङिसर्वनामस्थानयोः — the ऋ-stem takes गुण (अर्) in the strong cases; पितृ → पितर्

notes.text: पितर् + अम् → पितरम्

readings.vyakhya: सर्वनामस्थाने ऋतः गुणः। पितृ → पितर् → पितरम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: In the strong cases the ऋ rises to its गुण grade अर्: पितृ → पितर्, giving पितरम् for the accusative. This is the same गुण principle as the इ-stem's अग्नये — इ→ए there, ऋ→अर् here. One rule of strengthening, each vowel-class to its own grade.

readings.translation: He goes to the village.
readings.teaches: the pronoun तद् — सर्वनाम class; nom.sg masc सः

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि — सर्व, तद्, यद्… are the सर्वनाम (pronouns)
त्यदादीनामः — तद् takes अ before the ending (त् + अ + स् → सः, nom.sg masc)

readings.vyakhya: तच्छब्दः सर्वनाम। पुंसि प्रथमैकवचने सः।
readings.vyakhya_en: तद् is a सर्वनाम (pronoun) — its own declension-class. In the masculine nominative singular it is सः, "he / that one." You have met अहम् (I) and त्वम् (you); तद् supplies the third person, and stands in for any masculine noun.

readings.translation: The man gives fruit to him.
readings.teaches: the सर्वनाम special dative — स्मै, giving तस्मै (not the noun -आय)

notes.role: सर्वनाम्नः स्मै — an अ-stem pronoun's dative ending becomes स्मै; तद् + स्मै → तस्मै

readings.vyakhya: सर्वनाम्नः ङेः स्मै। बालाय इति नाम, तस्मै इति सर्वनाम।
readings.vyakhya_en: Where the noun बाल took -आय (बालाय, ex005), the pronoun takes a special dative -स्मै: तस्मै, "to him." This स्मै marks the सर्वनाम class — the pronouns decline by their own rules, and तस्मै/यस्मै/कस्मै all share it.

readings.translation: Who studies, he knows. (He who studies, knows.)
readings.teaches: relative–correlative यः … सः — the core Sanskrit clause-linker

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि — यद् is a सर्वनाम; declines like तद् (यः, यस्मै…)

notes.text: the correlative answering यः

readings.vyakhya: यः इति सम्बन्धः, सः इति प्रतिसम्बन्धः। यत्-तद्-नित्यसम्बन्धः।
readings.vyakhya_en: Sanskrit links clauses with a relative–correlative pair: यः ("who") in the first clause is answered by सः ("he") in the second — "who studies, he knows." यद् and तद् decline alike and travel together; this यः … सः frame is how Sanskrit builds the relative clauses that pervade real prose.

readings.translation: The teacher tells the lesson.
readings.teaches: a उ-stem masculine: nom गुरुः (parallel to अग्निः)

notes.text: गुरु + सु → गुरुः, just as अग्नि + सु → अग्निः

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → पाठम्

readings.vyakhya: उकारान्तं पुंलिङ्गम् गुरुशब्दः। प्रथमायाम् गुरुः, यथा अग्निः।
readings.vyakhya_en: गुरु ends in उ, as अग्नि ends in इ — and they decline alike. The nominative singular is गुरुः, formed exactly as अग्निः was. The उ-stem differs from the इ-stem only in which vowel it carries, not in how it behaves.

readings.translation: He gives fruit to the teacher.
readings.teaches: the उ-stem dative गुरवे — उ takes गुण (उ → ओ → अव्) by the SAME rule as अग्नये

notes.role: चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → the recipient गुरु takes चतुर्थी

notes.en: the grade ओ (उ → ओ, written अव् before the vowel)

notes.role: घेर्ङिति — the SAME rule that gave अग्नये; before a ङित् ending the उ-stem takes गुण; गुरु + ए → गुरवे

readings.vyakhya: घेः ङिति गुणः — इकारे एकारः, उकारे ओकारः। अग्नये, गुरवे।
readings.vyakhya_en: The one rule घेर्ङिति strengthens both classes before the dative: इ → ए gave अग्नये; उ → ओ gives गुरवे (the ओ written as अव् before the following vowel). One principle of गुण, each vowel to its own grade — अग्नये and गुरवे are the same move on different vowels.

readings.translation: The king goes.
readings.teaches: न-stem राजन् — the bare पद loses its final न् → राजा

notes.role: स्वतन्त्रः कर्ता → राजन् is the agent
प्रथमा for the bare prātipadika-sense

notes.text: राजन् + सु; the सु drops, leaving the पद राजन्

notes.role: नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य → a पद-final न् drops → राजा (with lengthening, 6.4.8)
सर्वनामस्थाने चासम्बुद्धौ → the penultimate आ-lengthening that gives राजा

readings.vyakhya: प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य नकारस्य लोपः। राजन् → राजा। पदान्ते न् न तिष्ठति।
readings.vyakhya_en: Consonant stems behave differently from the vowel stems you have met. राजन् ("king") ends in न् — but a word-final (पद-final) न् DROPS (8.2.7), and the penultimate lengthens (6.4.8), so the nominative is राजा, not *राजन्*. The stem hides its न् whenever it stands bare at a word's end. This single न-loss shapes the whole paradigm.

readings.translation: He sees the king.
readings.teaches: राजन् accusative — a STRONG (सर्वनामस्थान) ending keeps न् and lengthens → राजानम्

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → राजानम्

notes.text: राजन् + अम्; अम् is a सर्वनामस्थान (strong) ending — the न् stays

notes.role: सर्वनामस्थाने चासम्बुद्धौ → before a strong ending the penultimate lengthens → राजान् → राजानम्

readings.vyakhya: सर्वनामस्थाने नकारः तिष्ठति, उपधा च दीर्घा। राजन् + अम् → राजानम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: Where the bare पद lost its न्, a *strong* ending (सर्वनामस्थान — the nom./acc. endings) keeps it and lengthens the vowel before it (6.4.8): राजन् + अम् → राजानम्. So the king is राजा when bare, राजानम् as object. The consonant stem is "strong" (full न्, long vowel) before some endings and "weak" before others — the split that defines this whole family.

readings.translation: The king's son.
readings.teaches: राजन् weak/oblique — before a vowel ending the अ of अन् drops → राज्ञः

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे → the relational genitive → राज्ञः

notes.text: राजन् + अस् (gen.sg); this is a भ weak base before a vowel ending

notes.role: अल्लोपोऽनः → in a भ stem the अ of अन् drops → राज्ञ् + अस् → राज्ञः

readings.vyakhya: भसंज्ञके अनो अकारलोपः। राजन् + अस् → राज्ञः। दुर्बले अङ्गे न तिष्ठति अकारः।
readings.vyakhya_en: The third face of राजन्: before a vowel-initial weak ending (the भ base), the अ of -अन् itself drops (6.4.134), giving राज्ञ्- — so the genitive is राज्ञः "of the king." Now the full pattern stands: राजा (bare, न-loss), राजानम् (strong, full + long), राज्ञः (weak, अ-loss). One stem, three shapes, each triggered by the ending's strength — the heart of consonant declension.

readings.translation: The mind is pure.
readings.teaches: अस्-stem neuter मनस् — प्रथमा = द्वितीया, final स् → visarga

notes.en: neuter (an अस्-stem; nom. = acc., like फल)

notes.text: मनस् bare पद; final स् → रु → visarga before pause

notes.role: ससजुषो रुः → word-final स् → रु → मनः
नपुंसकस्य झलचः — context for neuter forms (नुम् where due); here शुद्धम् stands nom.=acc.

readings.vyakhya: अकारान्तवत् नपुंसके प्रथमा द्वितीया च समे। मनस् → मनः, सान्तस्य रुत्वम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: Another consonant family: the अस्-stems, here neuter मनस् ("mind"). Like every neuter, its nominative equals its accusative (मनः = मनः). The final स् of the bare word becomes रु → visarga (8.2.66, the same tail that gave नरः), so मनस् surfaces as मनः. The strengthening (अस् → आस् before strong endings, by 6.4.14) appears in the oblique — मनांसि "minds" — the next cell to add.

readings.translation: The fruit is seen by the man.
readings.teaches: a-stem masc. नर तृतीया एकवचन = नरेण — टा→इन (7.1.12) + णत्व

notes.en: agent expressed by the instrumental (of the passive दृश्यते)

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया — the agent of the passive दृश्यते takes तृतीया
टाङसिङसामिनात्स्याः — after an a-stem, तृतीया टा → इन → नर + इन = नरेन
रषाभ्यां नो णः समानपदे — within one word the र turns the following न → ण → नरेण

notes.text: a passive (कर्मणि प्रयोग); its agent stands in तृतीया → नरेण

readings.vyakhya: नरशब्दात् तृतीयैकवचने टा, सा अकारात् परा इनादेशम् (७.१.१२), ततो रेफात् नकारस्य णत्वम् (८.४.१), इति नरेण।
readings.vyakhya_en: For नर in the instrumental singular the ending is टा; after an a-stem टा becomes इन (7.1.12), giving नरेन. The र then retroflexes the following न to ण (णत्व, 8.4.1) — नरेण. As the agent of the passive दृश्यते "is seen," it stands in the तृतीया (2.3.18).

readings.translation: The man comes from the village.
readings.teaches: अपादान/पञ्चमी singular — ङसि → आत् after the a-stem → ग्रामात्

notes.text: नरः → नरो before the voiced ग (visarga सन्धि)

notes.en: the fixed point from which departure happens

notes.role: ध्रुवमपायेऽपादानम् — the fixed point one moves away from is अपादान
अपादाने पञ्चमी — the अपादान takes पञ्चमी
टाङसिङसामिनात्स्याः — after an a-stem ङसि → आत् → ग्रामात्

readings.vyakhya: ग्रामो ध्रुवम् अपायस्य, ततो नरस्य आगमनम्। अतो ग्रामात् इति अपादाने पञ्चमी; अकारान्तत्वात् ङसेः आत्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The village is the fixed point the man moves away from, so it is अपादान (1.4.24), expressed by the पञ्चमी (2.3.28). Because the stem ends in अ, the ablative ending ङसि becomes आत् (7.1.12) → ग्रामात् "from the village."

readings.translation: The man is in the village.
readings.teaches: सप्तमी (locative) singular — the अधिकरण as locus → ग्रामे

notes.en: locus — the substratum of the action

notes.role: आधारोऽधिकरणम् — the locus (आधार) is termed अधिकरण
सप्तम्यधिकरणे च — सप्तमी after the अधिकरण कारक

notes.text: ग्राम + ङि (loc.sg); the a-stem before ङि yields ग्रामे

notes.role: वर्तमाने लट् — present tense

readings.vyakhya: ग्रामे इति अधिकरणे सप्तमी। आधारोऽधिकरणम् इति संज्ञा, सप्तम्यधिकरणे च इति विभक्तिः।
readings.vyakhya_en: ग्रामे is the locus (अधिकरण) of the being: by आधारोऽधिकरणम् (1.4.45) the village as substratum gets the अधिकरण name, and सप्तम्यधिकरणे च (2.3.36) then assigns it the locative. The a-stem locative singular ending gives ग्रामे.

readings.translation: She goes to the river.
readings.teaches: तद् in the feminine — nom.sg सा (contrast masc सः)

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि — तद् is a सर्वनाम
त्यदादीनामः — तद् takes अ for its final (the base ता- in the feminine)
अजाद्यतष्टाप् — an a-stem feminine takes टाप् (आ); तद् → ता
हल्ङ्याब्भ्यो दीर्घात्… — the nom.sg सु drops after the long आ-stem → सा

readings.vyakhya: तच्छब्दः सर्वनाम। स्त्रियां टापा ता, सुलोपे सा।
readings.vyakhya_en: You met सः, the masculine "he" (ex045). Its feminine is सा. तद् takes the अ-base (7.2.102), then the feminine टाप् (आ, 4.1.4) gives ता-; the nominative सु drops after this long आ-stem (6.1.68), leaving सा. One pronoun तद्, two genders — सः and सा.

readings.translation: I go to the village.
readings.teaches: अस्मद् "I" nom.sg = अहम् — the suppletive nominative

notes.en: pronoun — अस्मद् ("I/we") is of the सर्व-class

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि — अस्मद् is a सर्वनाम
त्वाहौ सौ — before सु (nom.sg) अस्म् → अह; अस्मद् → अह + म् → अहम्

notes.text: so अहम् is suppletive — built on अह-, not the मद्/अस्म् stem of the oblique (मम, मया, मयि)

readings.vyakhya: अस्मच्छब्दः सर्वनाम। सौ परे अस्म् इत्यस्य अह इत्यादेशः — अहम्। मम मया मयि इति तु मद्-रूपम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: अस्मद् ("I/we") has the irregular nominative singular अहम्. By त्वाहौ सौ (7.2.94), before the nom.sg ending सु the portion अस्म् is replaced by अह — अस्मद् → अहम्. This is suppletion: अहम् is built on a stem found nowhere else, while every oblique case of "I" uses the मद्/अस्म् material — मम, मया, मयि.

readings.translation: The king of the gods shines.
readings.teaches: a-stem masc. षष्ठी plural — आम् takes नुट् → नाम्, vowel lengthens, न → ण

notes.en: the genitive of relation/possession (the शेष relation)

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे — the षष्ठी for the leftover relation, here "of the gods"
ह्रस्वनद्यापो नुट् — after a short-vowel/नदी/आप् stem, आम् takes the नुट् augment → नाम्
नामि — before नाम्, the stem-final vowel lengthens → देवा
अट्कुप्वाङ्नुम्व्यवायेऽपि — णत्व applies across the intervening vowels → देवानाम्

readings.vyakhya: देवानाम् इति षष्ठीबहुवचनम् — आमि नुट् (नाम्), नामि पूर्वस्य दीर्घः, रेफात् परस्य नस्य णत्वम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: देवानाम् is the genitive plural. The ending आम् first takes the नुट् augment न (7.1.54) → नाम्; before नाम् the stem-vowel lengthens to देवा (6.4.3, नामि); finally the र retroflexes the न to ण across the intervening vowels (8.4.2) → देवानाम्. With राजा (nom. sg.) the phrase means "the king of the gods shines."

readings.sentence: देवः देवौ देवाः। देवम् देवौ देवान्। देवेन देवाभ्याम् देवैः। देवाय देवाभ्याम् देवेभ्यः। देवात् देवाभ्याम् देवेभ्यः। देवस्य देवयोः देवानाम्। देवे देवयोः देवेषु। हे देव हे देवौ हे देवाः॥
readings.translation: The complete declension of देव "god" (a-stem masculine) — eight cases × three numbers.
readings.teaches: the FULL अकारान्त पुंलिङ्ग table — every cell of देव, with the सूत्र behind each ending (concepts already introduced; here gathered as a reference paradigm)

notes.role: स्वौजस्… — सु, the nom. sg. सुप् affix
ससजुषो रुः — final स् → रु → visarga → देवः
प्रथमयोः पूर्वसवर्णः — अ + औ (the dual ending) → औ → देवौ
प्रथमयोः पूर्वसवर्णः — अ + जस् (अस्) → आः → देवाः
अमि पूर्वः — अ + अम् → अम् → देवम्

words.gloss: द्वितीया द्वि — acc. dual (= nom. dual)

notes.text: acc. dual = nom. dual (औट् → औ), one form देवौ

notes.role: तस्माच्छसो नः पुंसि — masc. शस् → आन् → देवान्
टाङसिङसामिनात्स्याः — a-stem टा → इन → देवेन

words.gloss: तृ/च/पं द्वि — instr/dat/abl dual (भ्याम्); ONE form for all three

notes.role: सुपि च — अ → आ before भ्याम् → देवाभ्याम् (covers तृतीया/चतुर्थी/पञ्चमी dual)
अतो भिस ऐस् — a-stem भिस् → ऐस् → देवैः
ङेर्यः — a-stem ङे → य; + सुपि च (अ→आ) → देवाय

words.gloss: च/पं बहु — dat/abl pl. (भ्यस्); ONE form for both

notes.role: बहुवचने झल्येत् — अ → ए before भ्यस् → देवेभ्यः (covers चतुर्थी/पञ्चमी pl.)
टाङसिङसामिनात्स्याः — a-stem ङसि → आत् → देवात्
टाङसिङसामिनात्स्याः — a-stem ङस् → स्य → देवस्य

words.gloss: ष/स द्वि — gen/loc dual (ओस्); ONE form for both

notes.role: ओसि च — अ → ए before ओस् → देवयोः (covers षष्ठी/सप्तमी dual)
ह्रस्वनद्यापो नुट् — आम् takes नुट् → नाम्
नामि — vowel lengthens before नाम् → देवानाम्
बहुवचने झल्येत् (and the loc.sg ए-result) → देवे

words.gloss: सप्तमी बहु — loc. pl. (सुप् → सु; स → ष)

notes.role: बहुवचने झल्येत् — अ → ए before सु → देवे
आदेशप्रत्ययोः — स् → ष् after the इण् ए → देवेषु
सम्बोधने च — the vocative; sg. is the bare stem → हे देव

readings.vyakhya: अकारान्तस्य पुंलिङ्गस्य (देव) सर्वाः विभक्तयः सर्वाणि वचनानि च — एकत्र दर्शिताः। एकैकं सूत्रं प्रत्येकं प्रत्ययम् आदेशं च साधयति।
readings.vyakhya_en: You met प्रथमा through सप्तमी one cell at a time (ex001–ex013). Here is the WHOLE a-stem masculine paradigm of देव in one place — the reference table the readings were building toward. Read down each column for a number (sg · dual · pl), across each row for a case. Note the economies Pāṇini builds in: the dual collapses three oblique cases into देवाभ्याम् and two more into देवयोः; the plural shares देवेभ्यः for dative and ablative. Every other a-stem masculine — नर, राम, बाल, पुत्र, अश्व — declines exactly thus; learn देव and you hold them all. Each cell names the sūtra that shapes its ending, so the table doubles as an index into the अङ्ग-operations of adhyāyas 6–7.

chapters.title: तिङ् — verbal conjugation: पुरुष × वचन × लकार

readings.translation: I go to the village.
readings.teaches: person (पुरुष): the उत्तमपुरुष — speaker — selects a different ending

notes.text: the pronoun for the speaker

notes.role: तिङस्त्रीणि त्रीणि प्रथममध्यमोत्तमाः — the तिङ् endings fall into three पुरुष: प्रथम, मध्यम, उत्तम
तिप्तस्झि… — the तिङ् ending मिप् for उत्तम·एक → गच्छामि

readings.vyakhya: वक्ता उत्तमपुरुषः। एकस्मिन् कर्तरि एकवचनम् — गच्छामि।
readings.vyakhya_en: The speaker is the उत्तमपुरुष. The verb's ending names who acts, just as the noun's ending named its role: गच्छति (he goes) and गच्छामि (I go) share one root, one tense — only the पुरुष differs.

readings.translation: You go to the village.
readings.teaches: person: the मध्यमपुरुष — the one addressed

notes.text: the pronoun for the one addressed

notes.role: तिङ् ending सिप् for मध्यम·एक → गच्छसि

readings.vyakhya: यम् प्रति उच्यते सः मध्यमपुरुषः।
readings.vyakhya_en: The one spoken to is the मध्यमपुरुष. Three persons now stand together: गच्छति (प्रथम, he), गच्छसि (मध्यम, you), गच्छामि (उत्तम, I) — one root, three endings.

readings.translation: The boy went to the village.
readings.teaches: tense (लकार): the past — लङ् replaces लट्, and an augment अ is prefixed

notes.role: अनद्यतने लङ् — for past (not of today) the लङ् replaces लट्

notes.text: अ-augment + गच्छ + त् → अगच्छत्

readings.vyakhya: भूते अनद्यतने लङ्। धातुः स एव, कालः अन्यः।
readings.vyakhya_en: For the past, the लङ् stands where the present लट् stood. The root is the same √गम्; only the tense — the लकार — has changed. गच्छति (goes) → अगच्छत् (went): a new tense-slot, marked by the अ-augment in front.
readings.note: // The full augment/ending derivation (3.4.100ff, 6.4.71) is later; here we state the siddha form अगच्छत् and cite the लकार choice 3.2.111. Stepwise derivation deferred to a Track-B path.

readings.translation: The man cooks rice.
readings.teaches: the verb's ending is परस्मैपद — the active-voice set of तिङ् endings

notes.en: active voice — the तिप्-तस्-झि set of endings

notes.role: लः परस्मैपदम् — the तिङ् endings replacing a लकार are by default परस्मैपद

readings.vyakhya: लादेशाः परस्मैपदम् — तिप्तस्झ्यादयः।
readings.vyakhya_en: The endings that replace a लकार are, in general, परस्मैपद — the active set (तिप्, तस्, झि …). पचति is one of them. A second set, the आत्मनेपद, stands beside it for the middle voice.

readings.translation: The man cooks rice (for himself).
readings.teaches: the आत्मनेपद — the middle-voice set, action for the agent's own sake

notes.en: middle voice — the त-आताम्-झ set of endings

notes.role: तङानावात्मनेपदम् — the तङ् (and शानच्/कानच्) replacements are आत्मनेपद
तान्येकवचन… — the nine endings distribute as 3 पुरुष × 3 वचन (एक/द्वि/बहु)

readings.vyakhya: पचति परस्मैपदम्, पचते आत्मनेपदम् — स एव धातुः, फलम् अन्यत्र वा स्वे वा।
readings.vyakhya_en: One root, two ending-sets. पचति (परस्मैपद) cooks for another; पचते (आत्मनेपद) cooks for oneself. The nine endings of each set fill the same grid — three पुरुष across three वचन — so a verb-form names person, number, and voice all at once.

readings.translation: He did that (long ago / it is told).
readings.teaches: लिट् — the perfect, for remote or reported past; the root reduplicates

notes.en: perfect — the remote or reported past (परोक्ष)

notes.role: परोक्षे लिट् — for a past beyond direct witness, लिट् replaces the लकार

notes.text: कृ reduplicates → च-कार → चकार

readings.vyakhya: परोक्षे भूते लिट्। धातुः द्विरुक्तः — चकार।
readings.vyakhya_en: For a past the speaker did not witness — the deep past of story and report — the लिट् is used, and the root doubles its first syllable: कृ → चकार, "he did" (out of sight, or long ago). Compare अकरोत् (लङ्, the past one saw): same act, different reach into time.

readings.translation: He will do that tomorrow.
readings.teaches: लृट् — the future; built on the root with a स्य-marker

notes.text: the adverb fixing the time as future

notes.role: लृट् शेषे च — for what is yet to be, लृट् is used

notes.text: करि + ष्य + ति → करिष्यति

readings.vyakhya: भविष्यति लृट्। करोति, अकरोत्, चकार, करिष्यति — एकः धातुः, चत्वारः कालाः।
readings.vyakhya_en: For what is still to come, the लृट् is used. Now the whole time-axis stands on one root √कृ: करोति (does), अकरोत् (did, witnessed), चकार (did, long ago), करिष्यति (will do). The लकार is the verb's clock — choose it, and the tense is set.

readings.translation: Let him go to the village. / He must go.
readings.teaches: लोट् — the imperative, for a command

notes.role: लोट् च — for an injunction (विधि), the लोट् is used

readings.vyakhya: विध्यादौ लोट्। गच्छति कथनम्, गच्छतु आज्ञा।
readings.vyakhya_en: Where गच्छति merely reports "he goes," the लोट् commands: गच्छतु, "let him go / he must go." The verb stops describing and starts directing. The same root, a mood instead of a tense.

readings.translation: He should go to the village. / He might go.
readings.teaches: विधिलिङ् — the optative, for what ought to be or might be

notes.role: विधिनिमन्त्रण… लिङ् — for injunction, invitation, wish, request, the लिङ् is used

readings.vyakhya: विधौ लिङ्। गच्छतु निश्चिता आज्ञा, गच्छेत् विधिः सम्भावना च।
readings.vyakhya_en: The विधिलिङ् softens command into propriety and possibility: गच्छेत्, "he should go," or "he might go." Beside the blunt लोट् (गच्छतु, "go!"), the लिङ् carries ought, may, would — the mood of advice and supposition. Tense says when; mood says how the speaker stands toward the act.

readings.translation: He did that yesterday.
readings.teaches: लङ् — the imperfect, for a NON-today (अनद्यतन) past

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि → सः
अनद्यतने लङ् → the imperfect for a not-today past → अकरोत्
तिङ्: तिप् (3·sg) on the past base → अकरोत् (with अट्-augment)

readings.vyakhya: अनद्यतने भूते लङ्। ह्यः इति अनद्यतनकालः, अतः अकरोत्।
readings.vyakhya_en: Sanskrit splits the past three ways by *remoteness*. लङ् (the imperfect, 3.2.111) is the past that does NOT fall on the current day — hence ह्यः "yesterday" → अकरोत् "he did." The अ- prefix (अट्-augment) is the past marker you also saw in अगच्छत्. Same root √कृ as करोति "does," now in the not-today past.

readings.translation: He did that long ago.
readings.teaches: लिट् — the perfect, for a remote (परोक्ष) past beyond witness

notes.en: indeclinable — "of old" (marks the परोक्ष, beyond-sight, past)
perfect — remote past, not directly witnessed

notes.role: परोक्षे लिट् → the perfect for a past beyond the speaker's witness → चकार (reduplicated)

readings.vyakhya: परोक्षे भूते लिट्। अदृष्टं चिरातीतं — चकार। तदेव कृ-धातुः, द्विरुक्तम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The perfect (लिट्, 3.2.115) is the *remote* past — परोक्ष, "beyond the eye," what the speaker did not himself witness (history, legend, "long ago"). √कृ reduplicates to चकार "he did (of old)." Contrast ex060: अकरोत् (लङ्) is yesterday's deed, चकार (लिट्) is the ancient deed. The tense itself tells you how far back, and whether anyone saw it.

readings.translation: He did that today.
readings.teaches: लुङ् — the aorist, the tense-neutral past (and today’s past)

notes.en: aorist — the general past (and the past of today)

notes.role: लुङ् → the aorist for past sense → अकार्षीत्
च्लेः सिच् — the aorist takes the सिच् (s-aorist) marker (derivation deferred)

readings.vyakhya: भूते सामान्ये लुङ्। अद्यतनं भूतम् अपि लुङा — अकार्षीत्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The aorist (लुङ्, 3.2.110) is the *unmarked* past — it states a past act without committing to remoteness, and it is the proper past for *today's* events (अद्य "today" → अकार्षीत् "he has done"). √कृ now spans all three pasts: अकरोत् (yesterday, लङ्) · चकार (long ago, लिट्) · अकार्षीत् (today, लुङ्). The full form-building (सिच्, वृद्धि) is a Track-B derivation.

readings.translation: He will do that tomorrow.
readings.teaches: लुट् — the periphrastic future, for a NON-today (अनद्यतन) future

notes.en: periphrastic future — a future not on the current day

notes.role: अनद्यतने लुट् → the लुट् future for a not-today future → कर्ता (= कर्तृ + an understood अस्ति)

readings.vyakhya: अनद्यतने भविष्यति लुट्। श्वः इति अनद्यतनः, अतः कर्ता।
readings.vyakhya_en: Sanskrit splits the FUTURE too. लुट् (3.3.15) is the future that does NOT fall today — श्वः "tomorrow" → कर्ता "he will do." It is "periphrastic": the form कर्ता is literally an agent-noun ("(he is) a doer (tomorrow)"). Contrast करिष्यति (लृट्, the general future, ex028). Past and future each have a today/not-today split — the लकार is the verb's calendar.

readings.translation: He should do (it). / Let him do (it).
readings.teaches: विधिलिङ् — the optative, for what ought or may happen

notes.role: विधिनिमन्त्रणामन्त्रण… लिङ् → लिङ् in commanding/advising/permitting → कुर्यात्
तिङ्: the लिङ् 3·sg ending → कुर्यात्

readings.vyakhya: विध्यादिषु लिङ्। कर्तव्यम् इति अर्थे — कुर्यात्। तदेव कृ-धातुः, विधिलिङि।
readings.vyakhya_en: The optative (विधिलिङ्, 3.3.161) is the mood of *should* — duty, advice, permission, rule (विधि, निमन्त्रण, आमन्त्रण…). सः कुर्यात् "he should do / let him do." It is the mood in which Pāṇini's own rules are framed ("X should happen"). √कृ: करोति "does" (fact), कुर्यात् "should do" (norm). Tense says when; mood says how the speaker stands toward the act.

readings.sentence: सः कुर्यात् इति आशीः। क्रियात् सः।
readings.translation: May he do (it) — the blessing form kriyāt.
readings.teaches: आशीर्लिङ् — the benedictive, a distinct लिङ् for blessings

notes.en: benedictive — the लिङ् used specifically for a blessing (आशीस्)

notes.role: आशिषि लिङ्लोटौ → for a blessing, लिङ् (or लोट्) is used
लिङाशिषि → this लिङ् is the आशीर्लिङ् (distinct from the विधिलिङ्) → क्रियात्

readings.vyakhya: आशिषि लिङ् — आशीर्लिङ्। "भूयात्", "क्रियात्" इति आशीर्वादरूपाणि।
readings.vyakhya_en: A blessing has its own mood. For an आशीस् (benediction, "may you…") the लिङ् is used (3.3.173), and this benedictive लिङ् is formally distinct from the optative (3.4.116) — क्रियात् "may he do," भूयात् "may (he) be / may it prosper." So √कृ has two लिङ् forms: कुर्यात् "should do" (विधिलिङ्, the norm) vs क्रियात् "may he do" (आशीर्लिङ्, the blessing). The same mood-letter ल् branches by intent.

readings.translation: The man is (becomes) in the village.
readings.teaches: गुण of the root vowel — भू → भो → भव् before शप् gives भवति

notes.role: वर्तमाने लट् — present sense → लट्
कर्तरि शप् — when an agent is denoted, शप् (अ) is added after the root (the गण-1 vikaraṇa)
सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः — before शप् the root vowel takes गुण → ऊ → ओ → (before अ) अव् → भव्
तिप्तस्झि… — the तिङ् ending तिप् for प्रथम·एक → भवति

readings.vyakhya: भू इति धातुः। शपि परतः ऊकारस्य गुणः ओकारः, सोऽवादेशम् आपद्यते — भव्। तिपि भवति।
readings.vyakhya_en: The root भू "be." Before शप् (the अ-vikaraṇa of गण 1, by कर्तरि शप्), the root vowel ऊ takes गुण (7.3.84): ऊ → ओ, which before the following अ becomes अव् — भू → भव्. With the प्रथम·एक ending तिप्, the present is भवति. Compare गच्छति: same लट्, same तिप्, but भू shows its गुण where गम् does not.

readings.translation: The two men go to the village.
readings.teaches: number on the VERB — two agents take the तस् ending → गच्छतः

notes.role: द्व्येकयोर्द्विवचनैकवचने — for two, the द्विवचन
तिङस्त्रीणि त्रीणि प्रथममध्यमोत्तमाः — each triad of तिङ् endings is प्रथम/मध्यम/उत्तम
तान्येकवचनद्विवचनबहुवचनान्येकशः — within a triad the three are एक/द्वि/बहुवचन
तिप्तस्झि… — the तस् ending (प्रथम·द्वि) → गच्छतः

readings.vyakhya: द्वयोः कर्त्रोः द्विवचनम्। प्रथमपुरुषस्य द्विवचनं तस् — गच्छतः। एको गच्छति, द्वौ गच्छतः।
readings.vyakhya_en: Number lives on the verb too. नरौ are two, so the verb takes the द्विवचन ending: of the प्रथम triad तिप्-तस्-झि (1.4.101/102), the middle one तस् gives गच्छतः. Side by side: गच्छति (one goes), गच्छतः (two go) — same root, tense, person; only वचन shifts.

chapters.title: सन्धि — the sound-changes at word and morpheme joins

readings.translation: "curds, Indra" → दधीन्द्रः (curds-Indra)
readings.teaches: सवर्णदीर्घ — two like (सवर्ण) vowels merge into one long vowel

notes.text: दधि + इन्द्रः: इ meets इ

notes.en: homogeneous — vowels of the same place of articulation

notes.role: अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः — a simple vowel before a like vowel; the two become one long vowel

notes.text: → ई → दधीन्द्रः

readings.vyakhya: समाने सवर्णे अकः दीर्घ एकादेशः। इ + इ = ई।
readings.vyakhya_en: When a simple vowel (अक्) meets a homogeneous vowel — इ with इ, उ with उ, अ with अ — the pair fuses into the single long vowel of that class. दधि + इन्द्रः gives दधीन्द्रः: two इ become one ई.

readings.translation: "not here" → नेह
readings.teaches: गुण — अ/आ before इ/उ/ऋ yields the गुण vowel (ए, ओ, अर्)

notes.text: न + इह: अ meets इ

notes.role: आद्गुणः — when अ/आ is followed by another vowel, the two become the single गुण vowel

notes.text: अ + इ → ए → नेह

readings.vyakhya: अवर्णात् अचि गुण एकादेशः। अ + इ = ए।
readings.vyakhya_en: An अ or आ followed by इ, उ, or ऋ does not merge to a long vowel but shifts to the गुण grade: अ + इ → ए, अ + उ → ओ, अ + ऋ → अर्. So न + इह → नेह. The same अ behaves differently depending on the vowel it meets.

readings.translation: "yours indeed" → तवैव
readings.teaches: वृद्धि — अ/आ before ए/ऐ/ओ/औ yields the वृद्धि vowel (ऐ, औ)

notes.text: तव + एव: अ meets ए

notes.role: वृद्धिरेचि — when अ/आ is followed by एच् (ए ऐ ओ औ), the two become the वृद्धि vowel

notes.text: अ + ए → ऐ → तवैव

readings.vyakhya: अवर्णात् एचि वृद्धिः एकादेशः। अ + ए = ऐ।
readings.vyakhya_en: When अ or आ meets one of the diphthong-grade vowels (ए, ऐ, ओ, औ), the result climbs to the वृद्धि grade: अ + ए → ऐ, अ + ओ → औ. So तव + एव → तवैव. गुण and वृद्धि are the two upward grades इ/उ already met in the verb.

readings.translation: "the wise one is to be served" → सुध्युपास्यः
readings.teaches: यण् — इ/उ/ऋ before an unlike vowel become the glide य्/व्/र्

notes.text: सुधी + उपास्यः: ई meets उ (unlike)

notes.en: the glides य् व् र् ल्

notes.role: इको यणचि — an इक् vowel (इ उ ऋ ऌ) before any vowel becomes its corresponding यण् glide

notes.text: ई → य् → सुध्युपास्यः

readings.vyakhya: इकः अचि यण् आदेशः। ई + उ → य् + उ = यु।
readings.vyakhya_en: When इ, उ, or ऋ meets an unlike vowel, it does not merge but turns into its glide — य्, व्, र् — and the following vowel stands: सुधी + उपास्यः → सुध्युपास्यः. (Like meeting like gave the long vowel of ex023; unlike gives the glide here.)

readings.translation: "speech here" → वाग् अत्र
readings.teaches: जश्त्व — a word-final hard stop softens to its voiced counterpart

notes.en: the soft (voiced) stops ग् ज् ड् द् ब्

notes.role: झलां जशोऽन्ते — a stop at word's end becomes its जश् (voiced) counterpart; क् → ग्

notes.text: वाक् → वाग्

readings.vyakhya: पदान्ते झलां जश्। क् → ग्, यथा वाक् → वाग्।
readings.vyakhya_en: A hard stop standing at the end of a word softens to its voiced partner: क्→ग्, त्→द्, प्→ब्. So वाक् "speech" appears as वाग् before अत्र. The word's lemma is वाक्; its sentence-form follows the join.

readings.translation: "and that" → तच्च
readings.teaches: श्चुत्व — a dental meeting a palatal becomes palatal

notes.text: तत् + च: dental त् meets palatal च

notes.en: the palatal series श् च् छ् ज् झ् ञ्

notes.role: स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः — a dental (त-class/स) next to a palatal (च-class/श) turns palatal; त् → च्

notes.text: त् → च् → तच्च

readings.vyakhya: स्तोः श्चुना श्चुत्वम्। त् + च → च् + च = च्च।
readings.vyakhya_en: A dental sound touching a palatal is pulled into the palatal series: तत् + च → तच्च. The त् becomes च् to match the following च. Assimilation — the first sound takes on the place of the second.

readings.translation: "the forest laughs" → वनं हसति
readings.teaches: a word-final म् becomes anusvāra (ं) before a consonant

notes.role: मोऽनुस्वारः — a word-final म् before a consonant becomes anusvāra; म् → ं

notes.text: वनम् → वनं (before हसति)

readings.vyakhya: पदान्ते मकारस्य हलि अनुस्वारः। वनम् → वनं हसति।
readings.vyakhya_en: A म् at the end of a word, when a consonant follows, contracts to the anusvāra ं: वनम् हसति → वनं हसति. (Before a vowel, or at a true pause, the म् stays — so it is the following consonant that triggers the change.)

readings.translation: "by Rāma": रामेन → रामेण (न becomes ण after र)
readings.teaches: णत्व — न् becomes ण् after र्/ष् in the same word

notes.text: राम + इन (instr.sg ending ट्→इन): the न् stands after the र् of राम

notes.role: रषाभ्यां नो णः समानपदे → न् after र् or ष् in one word → ण् → रामेण
अट्कुप्वाङ्नुम्व्यवायेऽपि → the change still applies across an intervening vowel/guttural/labial (here the ए) → रामेण

readings.vyakhya: रेफात् परः नकारः णकारः समानपदे, अट्-व्यवधानेऽपि। रामेन → रामेण।
readings.vyakhya_en: Within one word, a न् turns cerebral (ण्) when an र् or ष् precedes it (8.4.1) — even when a vowel, guttural, or labial stands between them (8.4.2). So राम + the instrumental -इन gives रामेण, not *रामेन*: the र् of राम reaches across the ए to retroflex the न्. This णत्व is why we say रामायण, ब्राह्मणः, नारायण.

readings.translation: "Rāma the sixth" → रामष्षष्ठः (स/त-series cerebralised by ष)
readings.teaches: ष्टुत्व — स् and the dentals turn cerebral (ष्/ट-series) next to ष् or a cerebral

notes.text: रामस् + षष्ठः: a dental स् meets the cerebral ष्

notes.en: cerebralisation — स्/तवर्ग → ष्/टवर्ग in contact with ष् or a cerebral

notes.role: ष्टुना ष्टुः → स् and the dentals next to ष्/टवर्ग become ष्/टवर्ग → रामष्षष्ठः

readings.vyakhya: षकारटवर्गसन्निधौ सकारतवर्गयोः ष्टुत्वम्। रामस् षष्ठः → रामष्षष्ठः।
readings.vyakhya_en: Mirror of श्चुत्व (which palatalised before श्/च-series): ष्टुत्व *cerebralises*. A dental स् or त-series sound, meeting a cerebral ष् or ट-series sound, itself becomes cerebral (8.4.41). रामस् + षष्ठः → रामष्षष्ठः; तत् + टीका → तट्टीका. The articulation simply assimilates to its neighbour's place — the same logic as जश्त्व and श्चुत्व, one row over.

readings.sentence: सम् कृतम् → संस्कृतम् (सङ्… → the nasal homorganic).
readings.translation: "well-made" सम्+कृत → the nasal matches the following stop
readings.teaches: अनुस्वार → परसवर्ण — anusvāra becomes the nasal of the following class

notes.text: सम् + कृत: final म् → anusvāra (8.3.23), then the anusvāra may take the class-nasal

notes.role: मोऽनुस्वारः → word-final म् before a consonant → anusvāra (संकृत)

notes.en: the nasal homogeneous with the following sound

notes.role: अनुस्वारस्य ययि परसवर्णः → the anusvāra becomes the class-nasal of the following यय् consonant

readings.vyakhya: मकारः अनुस्वारः, सः ययि परसवर्णः। सम् + कृत → संकृत → सङ्… परसवर्णेन।
readings.vyakhya_en: A final म् before a consonant first becomes anusvāra (8.3.23, the rule that gave वनं); then that anusvāra may take the *homorganic* nasal — the nasal belonging to the following sound's class (8.4.58). सम् + कृतम् → संस्कृतम्; सम् + गतः → सङ्गतः (the guttural ङ् before ग). The nasal quietly tunes itself to whatever stop follows.

readings.translation: "homage to thee": the विसर्ग returns to स् before त
readings.teaches: विसर्ग → स् — a visarga becomes स् before a hard dental (खर्)

notes.text: नमः + ते: the visarga of नमः meets the त् of ते

notes.role: विसर्जनीयस्य सः → a visarga → स् before a खर् consonant → नमस्ते

notes.text: नमस् here is a गति/preverb-like form; 8.3.40 also fixes its स् → नमस्ते, नमस्कारः

readings.vyakhya: विसर्गस्य सकारः खरि। नमः + ते → नमस्ते। पुनः सकारः प्रत्येति।
readings.vyakhya_en: The visarga is not the end of the story — before a hard consonant (खर्) it can revert to स् (8.3.34): नमः + ते → नमस्ते, नमः + कारः → नमस्कारः. The final स् of नरः became visarga before pause (8.2.66 → 8.3.15); here the reverse environment pulls the visarga back to स्. Sandhi is contextual all the way down: the same sound shows different faces by what stands next.

chapters.title: समास — compounds: two words joined into one

readings.translation: the king's man (विग्रह: राज्ञः पुरुषः)
readings.teaches: तत्पुरुष — the LATER member is primary; the earlier qualifies it

notes.text: विग्रह: राज्ञः पुरुषः — "the man of the king"

notes.role: प्राक् कडारात् समासः — from here the combinations are named समास

notes.en: determinative — the second member is the head

notes.role: तत्पुरुषः — a compound whose second member carries the main sense is तत्पुरुष

readings.vyakhya: उत्तरपदार्थप्रधानः तत्पुरुषः। राजपुरुषः — पुरुषः प्रधानम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: In a तत्पुरुष the second member is the head and the first qualifies it: राजपुरुषः is a kind of पुरुष (man) — the king's. Resolve it (विग्रह) as राज्ञः पुरुषः, "the man of the king." The compound is whatever its last member is.

readings.translation: Rāma-and-Kṛṣṇa (विग्रह: रामः च कृष्णः च)
readings.teaches: द्वन्द्व — members are coordinate ("and"); none subordinate

notes.text: विग्रह: रामः च कृष्णः च

notes.role: चार्थे द्वन्द्वः — words standing in the sense of "च" (and) form a द्वन्द्व

notes.en: dual — two people, so the compound is dual

readings.vyakhya: उभयपदार्थप्रधानः द्वन्द्वः। रामः च कृष्णः च = रामकृष्णौ।
readings.vyakhya_en: A द्वन्द्व joins members that would each stand with "and" — none is subordinate, both are heads: रामः च कृष्णः च collapses to रामकृष्णौ, "Rāma and Kṛṣṇa." Two people, so the compound itself is dual.

readings.translation: the yellow-clothed one [Viṣṇu] (विग्रह: पीतम् अम्बरम् यस्य सः)
readings.teaches: बहुव्रीहि — neither member is the head; the compound points OUTSIDE itself

words.gloss: the one whose garment is yellow

notes.text: विग्रह: पीतम् अम्बरम् यस्य सः

notes.en: possessive / exocentric — denotes someone characterised by the members

notes.role: शेषो बहुव्रीहिः — the remaining kind of compound is बहुव्रीहि
अनेकमन्यपदार्थे — several words denoting ANOTHER thing (the possessor) form a बहुव्रीहि

readings.vyakhya: अन्यपदार्थप्रधानः बहुव्रीहिः। पीतम् अम्बरम् यस्य — सः विष्णुः।
readings.vyakhya_en: A बहुव्रीहि names neither member: पीताम्बरः is not "yellow" and not "garment" but the one who has a yellow garment — Viṣṇu. The sense lies OUTSIDE the compound (अन्यपदार्थ). Resolve with यस्य: "he whose (यस्य) garment is yellow."

readings.translation: near Kṛṣṇa (विग्रह: कृष्णस्य समीपम्)
readings.teaches: अव्ययीभाव — the FIRST member (an indeclinable) is primary; the whole is an अव्यय

notes.text: विग्रह: कृष्णस्य समीपम् — उप = "near"

notes.en: adverbial — the compound behaves as an indeclinable

notes.role: अव्ययीभावः — a compound headed by an indeclinable (here उप) is अव्ययीभाव

readings.vyakhya: पूर्वपदार्थप्रधानः अव्ययीभावः। उप कृष्णस्य समीपम् — सर्वम् अव्ययम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: In an अव्ययीभाव the first member — an indeclinable like उप ("near") — is primary, and the whole compound becomes an indeclinable itself: उपकृष्णम्, "near Kṛṣṇa," fixed in form. Four types, four answers to one question: which member carries the sense?

readings.translation: a great man (विग्रह: महान् पुरुषः)
readings.teaches: कर्मधारय — a तत्पुरुष whose members share one case (adjective + noun)

notes.text: विग्रह: महान् पुरुषः — "a man who is great"

notes.en: a तत्पुरुष of adjective + noun, both in the same case

notes.role: तत्पुरुषः समानाधिकरणः कर्मधारयः — a तत्पुरुष whose members are co-referential (same case) is कर्मधारय
विशेषणं विशेष्येण — a qualifier (महत्) combines with the qualified (पुरुष)

readings.vyakhya: समानाधिकरणः तत्पुरुषः कर्मधारयः। महान् च असौ पुरुषः च।
readings.vyakhya_en: A कर्मधारय is a तत्पुरुष where the two members refer to the SAME thing — adjective and noun, both nominative: महान् पुरुषः → महापुरुषः, "great man." Unlike राजपुरुषः (the king's man — two different things, genitive relation), here महत् simply describes पुरुष. (महत् → महा in the compound.)

readings.translation: the three worlds (विग्रह: त्रयाणां लोकानां समाहारः)
readings.teaches: द्विगु — a numeral-first तत्पुरुष, denoting an aggregate

notes.text: विग्रह: त्रयाणां लोकानां समाहारः — "the aggregate of three worlds"

notes.en: a numeral-first compound, naming a counted aggregate

notes.role: संख्यापूर्वो द्विगुः — a तत्पुरुष with a number (त्रि) as its first member is द्विगु

readings.vyakhya: संख्यापूर्वः तत्पुरुषः द्विगुः। त्रयाणां लोकानां समाहारः त्रिलोकी।
readings.vyakhya_en: A द्विगु is a तत्पुरुष whose first member is a numeral: त्रि (three) + लोक (world) → त्रिलोकी, "the three worlds" taken as one set. It names a counted aggregate — द्वि-गु itself means "worth two cows." Same तत्पुरुष frame (second member heads), special first member: a number.

chapters.title: पाठाः — real passages (Hitopadeśa → Purāṇa → Upaniṣad → Saṃhitā)

source.curated: first quarter (पाद a) of the verse, taken whole; rest of the śloka omitted

readings.translation: Knowledge gives humility.
readings.teaches: first REAL sentence — uses only grammar already met (आ-stem fem, कर्मन्, present verb)

notes.text: an आ-stem feminine (formed with टाप्)

notes.role: अजाद्यतष्टाप् — feminines like विद्या take टाप् (the आ-ending); विद्या stands in प्रथमा
वर्तमाने लट् → present tense
तिङ्: तिप् (3·sg) → ददाति
कर्तुरीप्सिततमं कर्म → विनय is the कर्मन्
कर्मणि द्वितीया → विनयम्

readings.vyakhya: विद्या कर्त्री, विनयः कर्म, ददाति क्रिया — सर्वं पूर्वोक्तम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: Your first real sentence, from the Hitopadeśa — and you can already read it. विद्या (knowledge) is the कर्तृ in प्रथमा; विनयम् (humility) is the कर्मन् in द्वितीया; ददाति (gives) is a present-tense verb. Every piece is grammar you have met on toy sentences; here it stands in real Sanskrit, unchanged.

source.curated: second quarter of the same verse as rd001; taken whole

readings.translation: From humility one attains worthiness.
readings.teaches: more of the SAME verse — adds the अपादान (पञ्चमी "from") in real text

notes.en: source — that from which one proceeds

notes.role: ध्रुवमपायेऽपादानम् — the starting point (humility, whence worthiness comes) is अपादान
अपादाने पञ्चमी → विनयात् (→ विनयाद् before the voiced य, by जश्त्व)
कर्तुरीप्सिततमं कर्म → पात्रता is the कर्मन्
कर्मणि द्वितीया → पात्रताम्

readings.vyakhya: विनयात् इति अपादानम्, पात्रताम् इति कर्म। एकस्माद् गुणाद् अन्यः फलति।
readings.vyakhya_en: The verse continues: from humility (विनयाद्, अपादान/पञ्चमी) one attains worthiness (पात्रताम्, कर्मन्/द्वितीया). Note विनयात् → विनयाद् — the final त् softens to द् before the voiced य (जश्त्व, the consonant-sandhi you met). Real text, real sandhi, all grammar you hold. The chain so far: knowledge → humility → worthiness.

source.curated: third quarter; taken whole

readings.translation: From worthiness one obtains wealth.
readings.teaches: third link of the same chain — the अपादान→कर्मन् pattern is now a rhythm

notes.role: ध्रुवमपायेऽपादानम् — the source (worthiness) is अपादान
अपादाने पञ्चमी → पात्रत्वात् (→ पात्रत्वाद् before the voiced ध, जश्त्व)
कर्मणि द्वितीया → धनम्

readings.vyakhya: पात्रत्वाद् इति अपादानम्, धनम् इति कर्म — स एव विधिः।
readings.vyakhya_en: The same shape a third time: from worthiness (पात्रत्वाद्, पञ्चमी) one obtains wealth (धनम्, द्वितीया). Once you see the अपादान→कर्मन् rhythm — "from X, attain Y" — the verse reads itself. पात्रत्वात् → पात्रत्वाद् again by जश्त्व before ध.

source.curated: fourth quarter, completing the verse; taken whole

readings.translation: From wealth, righteousness; from that, happiness.
readings.teaches: the closing link + elision of the repeated verb (understood आप्नोति)

notes.role: अपादाने पञ्चमी → धनात् (→ धनाद् before voiced ध, जश्त्व)

notes.text: धर्मम् → धर्मं (final म् → anusvāra before त, the sandhi you met)

notes.en: indeclinable adverb (= "from that", standing for तस्मात्)

readings.vyakhya: धनाद् धर्मः, धर्मात् सुखम् — क्रिया अनुवर्तते। विद्यायाः सुखपर्यन्तः क्रमः।
readings.vyakhya_en: The verse closes: from wealth, righteousness (धर्मं); from that (ततः), happiness (सुखम्). The verb आप्नोति is not repeated — it is understood, carried over (अनुवृत्ति) from the previous line, exactly as a sūtra carries words forward. You have now read a whole verse: विद्या → विनय → पात्रत्व → धन → धर्म → सुख, knowledge leading step by step to happiness.

source.curated: second hemistich only; the first (śatruṇā na hi sandadhyāt…, optative) omitted as harder

readings.sentence: सुतप्तम् अपि पानीयं शमयत्य् एव पावकम्।
readings.translation: Even well-heated water puts out fire.
readings.teaches: first Pañcatantra line; a complete vivid maxim, all known grammar + the particle अपि

notes.en: adjective qualifying पानीयम् (agrees with it — neuter, प्रथमा)

notes.role: स्वतन्त्रः कर्ता → पानीय (water) is the agent
अतोऽम् — neuter a-stem प्रथमा → पानीयम् (→ पानीयं, anusvāra before श)
वर्तमाने लट् → present
कर्तुरीप्सिततमं कर्म → पावक (fire) is the कर्मन्
कर्मणि द्वितीया → पावकम्

readings.vyakhya: पानीयं कर्तृ, पावकम् कर्म, शमयति क्रिया। अपि-शब्देन विरोधः सूच्यते।
readings.vyakhya_en: A complete Pañcatantra maxim, and it parses cleanly: पानीयं (water, कर्तृ/प्रथमा) शमयति (extinguishes) पावकम् (fire, कर्मन्/द्वितीया). The particle अपि ("even") + सुतप्तम् ("well-heated") carry the twist — even water that has itself been heated still quells fire. Real text, real rhetoric, grammar you hold.

source.curated: first hemistich only; second (dhanur vaṃśa-viśuddho…) omitted

readings.sentence: यस्य कस्य प्रसूतोऽपि गुणवान् पूज्यते नरः।
readings.translation: A virtuous man, though born of whomever, is honored.
readings.teaches: genitive relative (यस्य कस्य) + a passive verb (पूज्यते) in real text

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि — यद् is a सर्वनाम (pronoun)
षष्ठी शेषे — the relational genitive → यस्य

notes.text: यस्य कस्य together = "of no matter whom"

notes.en: agent (a past participle agreeing with नरः)

notes.text: प्रसूतः → प्रसूतो before अपि (visarga sandhi)
passive (कर्मणि प्रयोग) — "is honored", as भुज्यन्ते earlier

notes.en: agent (here the grammatical subject of the passive)

notes.role: स्वतन्त्रः कर्ता → नर

readings.vyakhya: यस्य कस्य प्रसूतः अपि — सम्बन्धः अनिश्चितः; गुणवान् नरः पूज्यते।
readings.vyakhya_en: The genitive pair यस्य कस्य ("of whomsoever") waives the question of birth; अपि ("even/though") concedes it; and the verse turns on पूज्यते — "is honored," a passive, the same कर्मणि form you met in नरैः फलानि भुज्यन्ते. The sense: a man of merit (गुणवान्) is honored whatever his lineage. A relative clause and a passive, working together in real Sanskrit.

source.curated: first hemistich; the connective 'tathā ca-' tag and the rest of the verse omitted

readings.sentence: न अग्निस् तृप्यति काष्ठानां न अपगानां महोदधिः।
readings.translation: Fire is not sated with logs, nor the great ocean with rivers.
readings.teaches: genitive plural (of-what one is sated) + a कर्मधारय compound (महा+उदधि) in real text

notes.text: the इ-stem अग्नि you declined (अग्निः); न+अग्निः → नाग्निः

notes.en: genitive — the thing one is sated OF

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे — the relational genitive; "sated of logs" takes षष्ठी

notes.en: compound — महा (great) + उदधि (ocean), adjective+noun same case

notes.role: तत्पुरुषः समानाधिकरणः कर्मधारयः — महा+उदधि is a कर्मधारय (महा+उदधि → महोदधि by सन्धि)

readings.vyakhya: अग्निः काष्ठानां न तृप्यति, महोदधिः अपगानां न — षष्ठी तृप्तेः विषये।
readings.vyakhya_en: Two parallel clauses: fire (अग्निः) is not sated of logs (काष्ठानां, genitive plural), the great ocean (महोदधिः, a कर्मधारय compound = महा "great" + उदधि "ocean") not of rivers. The genitive marks what one is sated *of*; the verb तृप्यति is shared across both halves. You now meet your own grammar — इ-stem, षष्ठी, कर्मधारय — in a real Pañcatantra verse.

readings.sentence: अ॒ग्निमी॑ळे पु॒रोहि॑तं य॒ज्ञस्य॑ दे॒वमृ॒त्विजं॑। होता॑रं रत्न॒धात॑मं॥
readings.translation: I praise Agni, the chosen priest, god, minister of the sacrifice, the invoker, lavisher of treasure.
readings.teaches: ACCENT debuts — the svara marks (॒ anudātta, ॑ udātta-context); grammar is known (accusatives in apposition + present verb)

notes.en: accent — the marks ॒ (anudātta, low) and ॑ (udātta/svarita); the underline on अ॒ is anudātta

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → अग्निम् (the इ-stem अग्नि you declined, here accusative)
तङानावात्मनेपदम् — ईळे is आत्मनेपद (the middle voice you met in पचते)

words.gloss: the one placed in front — the chosen priest

notes.text: padapāṭha shows the compound split: पुरः-हित (saṃhitā पुरोहितम्)

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे → यज्ञस्य

words.gloss: the sacrificing priest, minister of the rite
the invoker (the priest who calls the gods)

notes.en: an ऋ-stem (होतृ, like कर्तृ) in the accusative → होतारम्

notes.text: padapāṭha split रत्न-धातम (saṃhitā रत्नधातमम्)

readings.vyakhya: सर्वाणि कर्माणि अग्निविशेषणानि — द्वितीयायाम्। स्वराः उपरि अधश्च चिह्निताः।
readings.vyakhya_en: Your first Vedic verse, and the grammar is already yours: ईळे "I praise" governs a string of accusatives all in apposition to अग्निम् — पुरोहितम्, देवम्, ऋत्विजम्, होतारम्, रत्नधातमम् — "I praise Agni: priest, god, minister, invoker, treasure-giver." The ONE new thing is accent: the underline ॒ marks anudātta (low pitch), the stroke ॑ marks the raised/svarita pitch. Each word's accent is shown in its padapāṭha (isolated) form — पुरोहितं appears word-alone as पुरः-हितम्. Read it aloud with the pitches: this is how the Veda is chanted.

readings.sentence: अ॒ग्निः पूर्वे॑भि॒र्ऋषि॑भि॒रीड्यो॒ नूत॑नैरु॒त। स दे॒वाँ एह व॑क्षति॥
readings.translation: Agni, worthy to be praised by ancient seers and by new ones too — may he bring the gods here.
readings.teaches: second verse of the SAME hymn — अग्नि now नॉम (कर्तृ), instrumental-plural agents (the तृतीया, "by"), accent reinforced

notes.role: स्वतन्त्रः कर्ता → Agni is now the agent (नॉम, vs अग्निम् acc in verse 1)
कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → "by the ancient seers" takes तृतीया (the -भिः ending you met in नरैः)

notes.text: a gerundive (कृत्य) of ईड् "praise" — "fit to be praised"

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि → सः (he), the तद् pronoun
कर्मणि द्वितीया → देवान् (acc. plural)

notes.text: a future/subjunctive sense — "he will/may bring"

readings.vyakhya: अग्निः पूर्वैः नूतनैश्च ऋषिभिः ईड्यः; स देवान् इह आ वक्षति।
readings.vyakhya_en: The same hymn's second verse, and the frame holds: अग्निः is now the कर्तृ (nominative — last verse he was अग्निम्, the object). The seers who praise him stand in the तृतीया (पूर्वेभिः, ऋषिभिः, नूतनैः — "by the ancient, by the seers, by the new"), the same instrumental "by" you met in नरैः. ईड्यः is a gerundive — "to-be-praised." Then सः (he) देवान् (the gods, acc.) आ … वक्षति — "may bring here." One word, अग्नि, you now know in two cases and with its accent.

readings.translation: Through Agni one may win wealth and growth day by day — glorious, most rich in heroes.
readings.teaches: अग्नि now in the instrumental (अग्निना, "through/by"); the करण sense + an आम्रेडित (दिवेदिवे "day after day")

words.gloss: through Agni, by means of Agni

notes.en: instrument — that by which the gain is won

notes.role: साधकतमं करणम् — Agni is the करण (the most effective means)
कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → अग्निना (the इ-stem, now तृतीया — a third case for अग्नि)
कर्मणि द्वितीया → रयिम् (an इ-stem accusative, like अग्निम्)

notes.text: a subjunctive (लेट्) sense — "may/shall win"

notes.en: object (a second thing won, alongside रयिम्)

notes.text: an आम्रेडित — the word दिवे doubled (दिवे-दिवे) to mean "day after day"

notes.en: adjective qualifying रयिम् (an अस्-stem in द्वितीया)

notes.text: padapāṭha splits वीरवत्-तम (saṃhitā वीरवत्तमम्)

notes.en: superlative adjective qualifying रयिम् (a वत्-stem + तम superlative)

readings.vyakhya: अग्निना इति करणम्, रयिं पोषं च कर्म। दिवेदिवे इति आम्रेडितम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: Now अग्नि steps into a third case: अग्निना, the तृतीया — "through Agni." You have met this stem as object (अग्निम्), as agent (अग्निः), and here as instrument (अग्निना): one इ-stem across three कारकas. Through Agni one wins रयिम् (wealth) and पोषम् (growth), both accusatives, qualified by यशसं वीरवत्तमं ("glorious, hero-rich"). दिवेदिवे — दिवे doubled — is an आम्रेडित, "day after day."

source.curated: complete verse, taken whole. Accent verbatim (traditional Devanagari svara) from sri-aurobindo.co.in

readings.sentence: अग्ने॒ यं य॒ज्ञम॑ध्व॒रं वि॒श्वतः॑ परि॒भूरसि॑। स इद्दे॒वेषु॑ गच्छति॥
readings.translation: O Agni, the sacrifice, the rite which you encompass on every side — that alone goes to the gods.
readings.teaches: a Vedic relative-correlative (यं … सः) + सम्बोधन (अग्ने, "O Agni") + a 2sg verb असि ("you are")

notes.role: सम्बोधने च — the vocative; अग्ने (a fourth use of अग्नि, now address)
सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि → यद् is a सर्वनाम

notes.text: padapāṭha splits परि-भू (saṃhitā परिभूः); परि "around" + भू "be"

notes.en: 2nd person — "you are" (the मध्यम you met in गच्छसि)

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि → सः
सप्तम्यधिकरणे च → देवेषु (सप्तमी, locative plural)

readings.vyakhya: अग्ने इति सम्बोधनम्; यं यज्ञं परिभूः असि, स इत् देवेषु गच्छति।
readings.vyakhya_en: A relative-correlative, Vedic style: यं … (यज्ञम् अध्वरं) … सः — "which sacrifice … that one." अग्ने is the सम्बोधन (vocative, "O Agni") — your fourth case-use of this one stem. असि is "you are," 2nd person (मध्यमपुरुष), matching the सम्बोधन. The sense: the rite that Agni encloses on every side (विश्वतः परिभूः) — *that one alone* (स इत्) reaches the gods (देवेषु, locative).

readings.sentence: अ॒ग्निर्होता॑ क॒विक्र॑तुः स॒त्यश्चि॒त्रश्र॑वस्तमः। दे॒वो दे॒वेभि॒रा ग॑मत्॥
readings.translation: Agni the invoker, wise in will, true, most brilliant in fame — a god, may he come with the gods.
readings.teaches: a chain of NOMINATIVE epithets (predication, no verb) + a बहुव्रीहि-type compound + तृतीया-of-accompaniment

notes.en: epithet (in apposition to अग्निः) — an ऋ-stem nominative होता

notes.text: padapāṭha splits कवि-क्रतु (saṃhitā कविक्रतुः); कवि "sage" + क्रतु "will"

notes.en: possessive compound — "(one) whose क्रतु is that of a कवि"

notes.role: अनेकमन्यपदार्थे — a बहुव्रीहि naming an external possessor

notes.text: padapāṭha splits चित्रश्रवः-तम; चित्र "bright" + श्रवस् "fame" + तम superlative

notes.role: सहयुक्तेऽप्रधाने → the accompanier takes तृतीया → देवेभिः ("with the gods")

notes.text: an aorist-subjunctive (लुङ्/लेट्) sense — "may he come"

readings.vyakhya: होता कविक्रतुः सत्यः चित्रश्रवस्तमः देवः — सर्वाणि अग्निविशेषणानि प्रथमायाम्। देवेभिः इति सहार्थे तृतीया।
readings.vyakhya_en: Verse 1 strung accusatives; this one strings NOMINATIVES. होता, कविक्रतुः, सत्यः, चित्रश्रवस्तमः, देवः — all प्रथमा, all naming अग्निः (predication, no copula needed). कविक्रतुः is a बहुव्रीहि: "(one) whose क्रतु is a sage's." Then देवेभिः is the तृतीया of accompaniment — "with the gods" — the सह-sense you met in पुत्रेण सह. आ गमत्: "may he come hither."

readings.sentence: यदं॒ग दा॒शुषे॒ त्वमग्ने॑ भ॒द्रं क॑रि॒ष्यसि॑। तवेत्तत्स॒त्यमं॑गिरः॥
readings.translation: Whatever good you will do for the worshipper, O Agni — that, indeed, is your truth, O Aṅgiras.
readings.teaches: the सम्प्रदान (दाशुषे "for the giver", चतुर्थी) + a future verb (करिष्यसि, लृट्) in real Vedic

notes.en: relative — here introducing the whole clause

words.gloss: for the worshipper, for the giver (of offerings)

notes.en: recipient — the one for whom the good is done

notes.role: कर्मणा यमभिप्रैति स सम्प्रदानम् → the worshipper is सम्प्रदान
चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → दाशुषे
सम्बोधने च → अग्ने
लृट् शेषे च → future → करिष्यसि (√कृ; 2sg, "you will do")
षष्ठी शेषे → तव ("your")

notes.en: vocative — a second address to Agni

readings.vyakhya: यत् भद्रं दाशुषे करिष्यसि, तत् तव सत्यम्। दाशुषे इति सम्प्रदाने चतुर्थी।
readings.vyakhya_en: A यत्…तत् sentence with two new turns. दाशुषे is the सम्प्रदान — the dative (चतुर्थी), "for the worshipper," the same "for whom" case you met in नमो देवेभ्यः. करिष्यसि is a FUTURE (लृट्), "you will do" — √कृ now in the future, 2nd person. Two vocatives frame it: अग्ने and अङ्गिरः (a name of Agni). The sense: whatever blessing you will do for the giver — *that* is your truth.

source.curated: complete verse, taken whole. Accent verbatim (traditional Devanagari svara) from sri-aurobindo.co.in

readings.sentence: उप॑ त्वाग्ने दि॒वेदि॑वे॒ दोषा॑वस्तर्धि॒या व॒यं। नमो॒ भरं॑त॒ एम॑सि॥
readings.translation: To you, O Agni, day by day, by night and dawn, we come in thought, bearing homage.
readings.teaches: first-person PLURAL verb (एमसि "we come") + वयम् "we" + तृतीया-of-means (धिया "by thought")

notes.role: सम्बोधने च → अग्ने

notes.text: the आम्रेडित दिवे-दिवे (met in rd010) — "every day"
padapāṭha splits दोषा-वस्तः; दोषा "at night" + वस्तर् "at dawn"

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → धिया (तृतीया of the ई-stem धी)

notes.text: a present participle (शतृ) agreeing with वयम् — "(we) bearing"

readings.vyakhya: वयं धिया नमो भरन्तः दिवेदिवे त्वा उप आ इमसि। एमसि इति उत्तमपुरुषबहुवचनम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The worshippers speak now in their own voice: वयम् "we," and एमसि (उप…आ…इमसि) "we come" — a 1st-person PLURAL verb (उत्तमपुरुष बहुवचन), the same person you met as -मि in गच्छामि, now plural. To you (त्वा, accusative) we come, day by day (दिवेदिवे), at night and dawn (दोषावस्तः), in thought (धिया, तृतीया of means), bearing homage (नमः भरन्तः). A whole sentence of grammar you already hold.

source.curated: complete verse, taken whole — the object-string of verse 7 continued. Accent verbatim from sri-aurobindo.co.in

readings.sentence: राजं॑तमध्व॒राणां॑ गो॒पामृ॒तस्य॒ दीदि॑विं। वर्ध॑मानं॒ स्वे दमे॑॥
readings.translation: (To you,) ruling over the rites, the guardian of truth, the shining one, growing in your own home.
readings.teaches: a string of accusative epithets (continuing rd014) + षष्ठी-plural (अध्वराणां "of the rites") + सप्तमी (स्वे दमे "in one’s own home")

readings.vyakhya: राजन्तं गोपां दीदिविं वर्धमानं — सर्वाणि कर्माणि (पूर्वस्या ऋचः त्वा-शब्दस्य विशेषणानि)। अध्वराणाम् ऋतस्य च षष्ठी; स्वे दमे इति सप्तमी।
readings.vyakhya_en: This verse has no new finite verb — it continues verse 7's "to you we come," piling accusative epithets onto that त्वा: राजन्तम् (ruling), गोपाम् (guardian), दीदिविम् (shining), वर्धमानम् (growing). Two participles (राजन्तम् active, वर्धमानम् middle) decline like nouns in the accusative. The genitives अध्वराणाम् (over the rites) and ऋतस्य (of truth) mark domain; स्वे दमे — सप्तमी — locates it: "in his own home." Cases you hold, stacked into Vedic praise.

readings.vyakhya: पिता सूनवे इव, अग्ने नः सूपायनः भव; नः स्वस्तये सचस्व। चतुर्थ्यः बह्व्यः — सूनवे नः स्वस्तये।
readings.vyakhya_en: The hymn closes with a prayer, dense with the चतुर्थी (dative): नः "for us," सूनवे "to a son," स्वस्तये "for well-being" — three datives, all the "for whom" case (सम्प्रदान). The heart is a simile: पिता इव सूनवे — "as a father (is) to a son." Two imperatives (लोट्) carry the request: भव "be!" and सचस्व "abide!" — the command mood you met in गच्छतु, here in real Vedic. With this you have read the whole first hymn of the Ṛgveda, end to end, with its accent.

readings.vyakhya: वायो इति सम्बोधनम्; आ याहि पाहि श्रुधि इति लोडर्थाः। सोमाः कर्तारः, तेषां पाहि — षष्ठ्यर्थे।
readings.vyakhya_en: A new hymn, a new god — but the grammar is the invocation pattern you just met closing hymn 1. वायो is the सम्बोधन (vocative of the उ-stem वायु, गुण → वायो like गुरो), and it is answered by a volley of imperatives (लोट्): आ याहि "come!", पाहि "drink!", श्रुधि "hear!". The Somas (सोमाः, nominative plural) stand ready (अरंकृताः); drink *of them* — तेषाम्, a genitive (षष्ठी) in the partitive sense — and hear the call (हवम्, accusative). The whole verse is address + command, the heartbeat of Vedic prayer.

readings.vyakhya_en: Hymn 1 ended with "we come"; here the worshippers are NAMED — जरितारः, "the singers," the agents (कर्तृ, an ऋ-stem nominative plural like कर्तारः). They praise (जरन्ते, 3rd-person plural) you (त्वाम्, accusative) with hymns (उक्थेभिः) — the तृतीया of means, the same "with/by" you met in नरैः and धिया. Two epithets describe them: सुतसोमाः ("Soma-pressed," a बहुव्रीहि) and अहर्विदः ("day-knowers"). All grammar you hold.

readings.vyakhya_en: A feminine subject leads: धेना ("stream," an आ-stem feminine like विद्या), with two feminine adjectives agreeing — प्रपृञ्चती ("nourishing") and उरूची ("broad"). It is तव ("yours," genitive) and it जिगाति ("goes") दाशुषे ("to the worshipper," dative). The last word shows a second flavour of the dative: सोमपीतये — *for the purpose of* Soma-drinking. One case (चतुर्थी), two senses: "to whom" (दाशुषे) and "for what" (सोमपीतये).

readings.vyakhya_en: The DUAL arrives — Sanskrit's third number, for exactly two. The pair इन्द्रवायू is a द्वन्द्व compound ("Indra and Vāyu") in the dual (द्विवचन, 1.4.22), and everything addressed to them is dual too: आ गतम् "come, *you two*" (a dual imperative), and वाम् "you two" (the dual of युष्मद्). Between, सुताः ("the pressed Somas") and इन्दवः ("the drops") are plural subjects. Singular, plural, and now dual — the वचन triad is complete, here in real Vedic.

readings.vyakhya_en: The dual you just met now drives the VERB. वायो and इन्द्रः, joined by च, are two — so चेतथः ("you two perceive") is a dual finite verb, तौ ("you two") is the dual pronoun, यातम् ("come, you two") the dual imperative, and वाजिनीवसू a dual vocative epithet. Everything addressed to the pair is dual. They take note सुतानाम् — "of the pressed Somas," a partitive genitive (षष्ठी). The whole verse is a drill in द्विवचन.

And the address नरा is नरौ — the DUAL of नर, the very first noun you ever declined, now standing in the vocative dual.

readings.vyakhya_en: A new divine pair enters — Mitra and Varuṇa. Here they are OBJECTS: मित्रम् … वरुणम् च, accusatives, "I call (हुवे, 1st-person singular) Mitra and Varuṇa," each with its epithet (पूतदक्षम् "pure-skilled," रिशादसम् "foe-destroying"). They jointly perfect धियं घृताचीम् ("the luminous thought," accusative) — and साधन्ता, "the two who perfect," is a participle in the DUAL, agreeing with the pair. The dual now appears even on a participle.

notes.role: चार्थे द्वन्द्वः → मित्रावरुणौ ("Mitra and Varuṇa")
द्व्येकयोर्द्विवचनैकवचने → dual → मित्रावरुणौ

words.gloss: O you two who increase the Truth

notes.text: padapāṭha splits ऋत-वृध्; ऋत "Truth" + वृध् "increasing"

words.gloss: you two who touch the Truth
